prompt: Match each key to what it is expected to do on an ordinary web page.
hint: The table in the first reading section.

pairs.right: moves the focus to the previous control
follows a link or presses a button
move between the options inside one control
closes a menu or a dialog that was opened

right_distractors: reloads the page from the server

prompt: Which element answers both Enter and Space with no script written for either?
hint: A link answers only one of them.

choices.text: A link, written <a href>
choices.why: A link follows on Enter; Space scrolls the page.

choices.text: A <button>
choices.why: Right. The browser gives a button both keys.

choices.text: A <div> with an onclick handler
choices.why: It cannot even take the focus.

choices.text: A <span> with tabindex="0" and the class button
choices.why: It can take the focus now, and still answers no key until somebody writes the code.

prompt: A page has one input with tabindex="3" and everything else at the default. Where does the first Tab go?
hint: Positive values come before document order.

choices.text: To the first link in the page, as always
choices.why: Any positive tabindex jumps in front of it.

choices.text: To the third focusable element in the markup
choices.why: The number is an order among positive values, not a position on the page.

choices.text: To that input, wherever it sits in the page
choices.why: Right. The only positive value is first, then the rest in document order.

choices.text: Nowhere: a positive value removes the page from the tab order
choices.why: Only the element's position changes; the rest stays reachable.

prompt: A modal dialog keeps the focus inside it while it is open. When does that fail 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap?
hint: Keeping the focus in is the intended behaviour.

choices.text: Whenever the focus cycles from the last control back to the first
choices.why: That cycling is what a modal should do while it is open.

choices.text: When neither Escape nor a control inside it closes it
choices.why: Right. A trap is a region the keyboard cannot leave at all.

choices.text: When it opens without moving the focus into it
choices.why: A defect, but the opposite one: the focus is left outside.

choices.text: When the page behind it cannot be reached with Tab
choices.why: While a modal is open the page behind is meant to be inert.

prompt: In the run against book2.html, what was the first stop of the tab order?

choices.text: The link What's on
choices.why: It came second, after the positive tabindex.

choices.text: The Show select
choices.why: That was stop 5.

choices.text: The name field
choices.why: Right: textbox "Your name", pulled to the front by tabindex="1".

choices.text: The Book control
choices.why: Book was never reached at all.

prompt: How many stops did tab.js count in book3.html before the focus left the page?
hint: From the skip link to the button.

prompt: tab.js prints "no focus outline" for a stop. What should the tester conclude?
hint: The check reads one CSS property.

choices.text: That the page fails 2.4.7, and the defect can be filed as it is
choices.why: Maybe; the page could draw focus another way the script does not read.

choices.text: That it is worth looking, since the page may draw focus some other way
choices.why: Right. A missing outline is an indicator, not a proof.

choices.text: That the element cannot receive the focus
choices.why: It did receive it; that is why it is in the list.

choices.text: Nothing, because outlines are a matter of design
choices.why: Some visible indicator is required at AA by 2.4.7.

prompt: Why does :focus-visible let a designer keep a clean look for mouse users?
hint: When does the browser apply it?

choices.text: Browsers apply it to keyboard focus, usually not to clicks
choices.why: Right. The ring shows when it helps.

choices.text: It hides the ring from sighted users and keeps it for screen readers
choices.why: Screen readers do not see outlines; the ring is for people who see the screen.

choices.text: It draws the ring on links, and usually on nothing else
choices.why: It applies to any focusable element.

choices.text: It replaces the outline with a background colour
choices.why: It is a selector; what it draws is whatever the rule says.

prompt: A cookie banner is fixed to the bottom of the window. Tabbing down, the focused link scrolls fully underneath it. Which criterion fails?
hint: The ring exists; it is under something.

choices.text: 2.4.7 Focus Visible
choices.why: An indicator exists; the problem is what is drawn over it.

choices.text: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap
choices.why: The focus can still move on; it is only hidden.

choices.text: 2.4.3 Focus Order
choices.why: The order is fine.

choices.text: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
choices.why: Right. The focused control is entirely hidden by content the page drew.

prompt: A skip link's target that is not focusable on its own is given tabindex="___", so following the link moves the focus there.
hint: Focusable by script, not by Tab.

prompt: Which criterion does a skip link serve?
hint: It is about blocks repeated on every page.

choices.text: 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks
choices.why: Right. A way past the logo and navigation on every page.

choices.text: 2.4.13 Focus Appearance
choices.why: That is about how big and how contrasting the indicator is.

choices.text: 2.1.1 Keyboard
choices.why: The page can be operable without one; the link saves effort.

choices.text: 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence
choices.why: That is about reading order in the markup.

prompt: In book3.html, why is the Book button inside the form with an onsubmit handler, rather than a button with onclick?

choices.text: onclick does not fire when a button is pressed with Enter
choices.why: It does fire; the browser turns Enter and Space on a button into a click.

choices.text: Enter in the name field then books too, like any form
choices.why: Right. And preventDefault stops the browser's own submission.

choices.text: A <button> outside a form cannot take the focus
choices.why: It can; a button is focusable anywhere.

choices.text: axe reports onclick handlers as violations
choices.why: No rule looks at handlers.

prompt: Put book3.html's first five tab stops in order.
audit.js reported 0 violations on both book2.html and book3.html. What does that pair of results show?
hint: One page cannot be booked from the keyboard.

choices.text: That the keyboard fixes changed nothing a user would notice
choices.why: They decide whether a keyboard user can book at all.

choices.text: That book2.html was already accessible
choices.why: tab.js showed it could not be booked without a mouse.

choices.text: That only the tab walk tells the two apart
choices.why: Right. The difference was invisible to every rule that ran.

choices.text: That axe ignores pages with a skip link
choices.why: It audited both pages in full.

prompt: A designer wants the cards of a grid shown in a new order on wide screens, using CSS order, without touching the HTML. What should the tester check?
hint: The tab order comes from the markup.

choices.text: Nothing: CSS changes appearance and never affects keyboard users
choices.why: The focus will follow the markup while the eye follows the screen.

choices.text: That every card has a positive tabindex matching its new place
choices.why: That puts the cards in front of the whole page and makes it worse.

choices.text: Whether Tab now jumps around the screen out of visual order
choices.why: Right. Focus order and reading order can part company, which 2.4.3 cares about.

choices.text: That axe's tabindex rule passes
choices.why: That rule only looks for positive values; CSS order is invisible to it.

prompt: A custom dropdown is a <div> listing twenty options, each with tabindex="0". It works with Tab and Enter. What is still wrong?
hint: Where should Tab go, and where should the arrows?

choices.text: Nothing; it can be operated from the keyboard, so it meets 2.1.1
choices.why: Operable, and twenty Tab stops to get past it.

choices.text: It should be one stop, with arrows moving between options
choices.why: Right. Tab moves between controls; arrows move inside one.

choices.text: tabindex="0" must be replaced by positive values in order
choices.why: Positive values would pull it in front of the whole page.

choices.text: Its options need a focus outline of at least 7:1
choices.why: 7:1 is AAA text contrast, not an indicator rule.

prompt: After a deploy, tab.js's list for book3.html gains a ninth stop, a new link in the header, and the expected-order test fails. What is the right response?
hint: Why does the expected list live in the test?

choices.text: Delete the order assertion, since it fails on harmless changes
choices.why: Then nobody looks at the order when it changes, which is when it breaks.

choices.text: Give the new link tabindex="-1" so the order is back as it was
choices.why: That makes the link unreachable from the keyboard.

choices.text: Check the new order makes sense, then update the list
choices.why: Right. The failure is the prompt for a person to look.

choices.text: Re-run the test until it passes, since tab order can be flaky
choices.why: The order is computed from the markup; it does not change between runs.
